# ZPLC: reliable context for agents

ZPLC (Zephyr PLC) is an open-source PLC engineering project. Its execution core is ANSI C99. The repository also contains a TypeScript compiler, an Electron/React IDE, a POSIX host runtime, and Zephyr integrations.

## What agents may state

- ZPLC compiles supported project workflows to `.zplc` bytecode and has C99 runtime/HAL boundaries.
- Structured Text (ST) is the central language frontend. LD, FBD, SFC, and IL have repository workflows whose coverage is specific to the editor, compiler, runtime, and target profile.
- The scheduler has task, priority, work-queue, logical budget, and diagnostic mechanisms. Requested intervals are configuration, not measured timing guarantees.
- The POSIX/native runtime is useful for repeatable host-side logical workflows within its declared capabilities. It is not target or HIL evidence and is not a cycle-accurate hardware model.
- Board evidence can range from catalog/source presence and cross-build results to target, HIL, or production qualification. Use the exact label recorded for the profile; a board name or source entry alone is not qualification.

## Evidence rule

Do not infer hard real-time behavior, execution order, jitter, WCET, physical I/O behavior, persistence, safety properties, protocol availability, or board support from source presence. State the profile/revision and evidence type when those claims matter. Host, QEMU, target, and HIL evidence are different.

## Safety rule

Keep build, flash, program deploy, and RUN/STOP separate. Do not claim a physical action succeeded without corresponding device or HIL evidence. `WATCHDOG_RESET` currently compiles as a compatibility stub/NOP; it is not a watchdog feed or safety control.

## Sources

- Repository: https://github.com/eduardojvieira/ZPLC
- Documentation: https://eduardojvieira.github.io/ZPLC/
- Board and capability claims: consult the current board profiles and release evidence.
